verdict.rationale: The evidence shows a few rail-specific fields on payment objects: ACH objects carry a `returned` status with return codes in the `error` field, card events include a `decline_reason`, and wire objects expose a `status`. Nothing documents a transaction feed with counterparty details, stable identifiers, or enrichment. missing for 10: counterparty fields on transactions, a documented transaction object schema, stable or idempotent transaction identifiers, merchant/category enrichment, broader rail metadata (wire/FedNow details), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, transaction data is rich enough to build on — counterparty details, rail-specific metadata, stable identifiers, and enrichment that makes a raw bank feed usable in-product

citations.quote: Treasury Prime updates the [ACH object](/reference/ach) status to `returned` and populates the `error` field with the appropriate return code.
Card events in this status will contain a value in the `decline_reason` field which outlines the reason the transaction was declined.
You can track the progress of a wire by checking the `status` attribute on the Wire Transfer object.
